title: The UI's sleep report counts as user activity, so the screen never dims, sleeps or turns off
scenario: The UI owns sleep now (ui_sleep.c). After dim_s of idle on H, enter(1) emits UI_IN_SLEEP(1). handle(EV_UI) calls app_io_activity() before on_ui(). The app's mirror is still ON and the last UI_WAKE was more than 1 s ago, so app_io.c:139-141 posts UI_WAKE and ui_sleep_wake() undoes the dim at once. Levels 2 and 3 and PWR-short screen-off fail the same way. app_io_screen_off() sets s_screen=OFF, then the UI's enter(3) emits UI_IN_SLEEP(3). ui_input_cb (app.c:1458-1461) sees the mirror is not ON and posts EV_WAKE, so screen_set(ON) lights the screen again about 50 ms later. Result: the backlight flickers every dim_s, the ambient screen and screen-off are never reached, PWR at H idle does not keep the screen off, and the battery drains.
fix: Handle UI_IN_SLEEP before the screen-state check in ui_input_cb: post only EV_UI, never EV_WAKE, and never swallow it. In handle(), skip app_io_activity() for EV_UI when e->i == UI_IN_SLEEP so that only app_io_ui_sleep() runs.
verify_note: I confirmed this in the code. ui_sleep.c enter(1) calls ui_emit(UI_IN_SLEEP,1), and ui_input_cb sends it as EV_UI because the mirror is still ON. handle() EV_UI (app.c:1322) then calls app_io_activity(). Nothing touches s_last_wake_post while the device idles, so app_io.c:139-141 posts UI_WAKE. ui.c:502 then runs ui_sleep_wake(), which sees level 1, resets to 0, fades the backlight back up and restarts the LVGL inactivity timer. Level 3 fails the same way. PWR-short calls screen_set(OFF), so s_screen=OFF and UI_SCREEN_OFF is posted. enter(3) emits UI_IN_SLEEP(3), and ui_input_cb (app.c:1458) posts EV_WAKE because the mirror is OFF. That calls screen_set(ON), which posts UI_WAKE and lights the screen again. Result: a short backlight dip every dim_s, while ambient mode and screen-off are never reached. STATUS.md leaves the dim, clock and screen-off row unverified.

title: PWR-hold power-off on USB re-asserts the power latch, cancels the screen-off and shows the USB toast on a dark panel
scenario: app_io_power_off() calls board_power_off() (backlight 0) and stores s_screen=OFF without telling the UI, so the UI sleep level stays 0. After PWR is released, dim_tick calls screen_set(ON), which posts UI_WAKE. At level 0, ui_sleep_wake() only calls lv_display_trigger_activity() and returns, so the backlight stays 0 and the 'Питание от USB' toast is invisible. Within 200 ms poll_touch sees LVGL inactivity below 250 ms and calls app_io_activity(). Because s_latch_off is set, that calls board_power_latch_on() and clears s_off_check and s_note_until, which cancels the 2 s step that turns the screen off. End state: the latch is on again, so unplugging USB no longer powers the board off. The panel stays black while the UI is live and touches still act. After dim_s the UI dim fade raises the backlight to 25 %, then to full (see flow-1).
fix: Post UI_SCREEN_OFF from app_io_power_off so the UI goes to level 3 and owns the backlight. Show the USB note through a path that restores the backlight. Do not treat LVGL activity from poll_touch as user activity while s_latch_off, s_off_check or s_note_until is set (only a real touch or button should re-latch).
verify_note: I confirmed the sequence. app_io_power_off sets s_screen=OFF with atomic_store and never posts to the UI, so the UI sleep level stays 0 and board_power_off() has already set the backlight to 0. After PWR is released, dim_tick reaches screen_set(ON). It posts UI_WAKE, and at level 0 ui_sleep_wake only calls lv_display_trigger_activity, so the backlight stays at 0 and the USB toast is invisible. poll_touch runs every 200 ms with a 250 ms threshold, so it is sure to see that activity. It then calls app_io_activity(), which, because s_latch_off is set, calls board_power_latch_on() and clears s_off_check and s_note_until. The latch is back on, so unplugging USB leaves the board running on battery with a dark panel and a live UI. Even if the step that turns the screen off were reached, screen_set(OFF) would hit the flow-1 loop, which re-latches as well.

title: The first translator turn after a language change uses the old pair, because the UI's save is still pending
scenario: ui_set_langs() calls ui_save_str() for tr_lang_a and tr_lang_b; that save is debounced 1.5 s and deferred while the UI state is REC, UPLOAD, THINK or SPEAK (ui_work.c:245). It then emits UI_IN_LANGS, whose app comment claims the pair was already saved. submit_clip and tr_langs() read the pair from settings, and the request leaves lang_a/lang_b NULL, so ai_client_submit also reads settings. Example: pair RU|EN, tap chip B and pick DE; the UI returns to H. Hold chip B within 1.5 s and speak German. The recording defers the save, and src = tr_lang_b = 'en' is forced. The model is told the clip is English inside an ru/en schema, so the translation is wrong while the chips already show DE.
fix: Call ui_save_flush() in ui_set_langs (key_done already does this for the key). Alternatively, send the new pair with UI_IN_LANGS, keep it in s_a, and use it for q.lang_a/lang_b, the forced src and the side mapping in on_result.
verify_note: The mechanism is real. ui_set_langs (ui_misc.c:107-109) only queues the save through ui_save_str. The save goes out 1.5 s later, and save_timer_cb holds it back while the UI state is REC, UPLOAD, THINK or SPEAK, for up to 20 s. submit_clip/tr_langs and ai_client_submit (ai_client.c:1067-1075, lang_a/lang_b NULL) read the pair from settings, so a recording that starts within 1.5 s of the pick uses the old pair. A chip tap opens LP straight from H and nav_back returns there, so the case can happen. The window is narrow, though: the recording has to start within about 1 s of returning to H, or within about 0.6 s for a chip, which needs a 400 ms hold. I downgraded it to low.

title: BOOT on the phone-setup (QR) screen shows 'Закройте настройку сети' instead of recording
scenario: ui.md 2.3 says BOOT on T_QR jumps to H and records. app_ptt_down calls ui_boot_down(), which only posts UI_GOTO HOME and returns true. The app then calls start_recording() synchronously, and ready() still sees portal_active(): the Q screen is not yet deleted, and its portal_stop() runs later in the UI worker. The result is show_error('PT', 'Закройте настройку сети'). The user is taken out of the setup, nothing is recorded, and an error card for a portal that is already closing is added.
fix: For a BOOT press from UI_CTX_QR, do not fail on RDY_PORTAL right away. Keep the press pending and start the recording on app_portal_changed(false), with a short timeout, or stop the portal synchronously before the readiness check.
verify_note: ui.md 2.3 (line 338) says BOOT on T_QR jumps to H and records. On the QR screen ui_boot_down (ui.c:561-564) only posts UI_GOTO HOME and returns true. app_ptt_down then calls start_recording right away, and ready() calls portal_active(). The portal is still running at that point: it stops only after the Q screen is deleted, in delete_cb, which runs ui_work(stop_job) (scr_qr.c:307-310) on the worker task. So every BOOT press on Q gives show_error PT 'Закройте настройку сети', and the user lands on H with an error card and no recording.

title: 'Не тот язык' re-sends the latest kept clip, not the turn open in the reader
scenario: scr_reader computes the forced side from the entry being viewed (other = entry side A ? B : A). rerun_clip() ignores which entry that is and re-sends s_a.clip_pcm, the last voice recording. Example: turn 1 was spoken in RU (side A) and turn 2 in EN (side B). The user opens RD for turn 1 and taps 'Не тот язык', so other = B. Turn 2's clip is re-sent forced to EN, the language it was already detected as, which duplicates turn 2 and leaves turn 1 uncorrected. After a typed translator turn (last_kind TEXT, clip_ok still true), the same button on the typed entry re-translates an unrelated older voice clip. During UPLOADING it also aborts the in-flight turn and re-sends that turn's clip.
fix: Record which turn or chat entry the kept clip belongs to. Pass the entry id with UI_IN_WRONG_LANG, and re-run only when it matches the kept clip and last_kind == TURN_VOICE; otherwise show a toast.
verify_note: Any translator turn bubble opens RD (scr_home.c:507-508, scr_hist.c:34-35). wrong_cb works out the forced side from the entry being viewed, but rerun_clip (app.c:747-764) always re-sends s_a.clip_pcm, which is the most recent voice clip. text_turn never clears clip_ok, so after a typed translator turn the button re-sends an older, unrelated voice clip. On an older entry it re-sends the latest clip with a side taken from a different turn. The spec says the clip is kept only 'until the next turn' (ui.md 1191), so the button should apply to that latest turn only.

title: Replay in the reader speaks the newest translation, not the one shown
scenario: scr_reader passes the entry id with UI_IN_REPLAY, but on_ui calls replay() and ignores the argument. replay() always speaks s_a.last_tr and last_tr_lang, the most recent translation. Example: after two translator turns, the user opens RD on the first turn to play it to the other person and taps ▶. The device speaks the second turn's translation in its language while the screen shows the first.
fix: Use the entry argument: replay only when the entry is the latest translated turn, or have the UI hand over that entry's translation text and target language (text2/dst) to speak.
verify_note: replay_cb passes s_entry with UI_IN_REPLAY, but on_ui (app.c:1196) calls replay() without the argument. replay() speaks s_a.last_tr and last_tr_lang, which are overwritten on every translator result (app.c:874-878). RD opens for any translated bubble, so ▶ on an older turn speaks the newest translation while the screen shows the older text.

title: Error-card dedupe compares only the card type, so different errors and errors in a cleared chat get no card
scenario: show_error skips the card when card == last_card within 20 s. UI_CARD_GENERIC covers PT, K0, M0, AI, P2, P5, 400, 403, 403m, 413, 422 and H4xx, so a second, different error within 20 s shows only the orb ERROR and the generic short text 'Ошибка'. Example: 413 'Запись слишком длинная', then P5 'ИИ отказался отвечать': the user never sees the second reason. last_card is also not reset by new_chat(), set_mode() or a successful turn. Example: a server-error card at t=0, then 'Новый разговор', then the same error at t=10 s: the empty chat gets no card and no 'Повторить' button.
fix: Deduplicate on the error id (and body) rather than the card type. Reset last_card in new_chat(), in set_mode() and after a successful result.
verify_note: show_error (app.c:351) suppresses the card when the card type matches and it is within 20 s. UI_CARD_GENERIC covers every id that is not in ERR_MAP (PT, AI, M0, 413, 422, H4xx …) plus K0, so a second, different generic error gets only the orb ERROR state. error_begin then shows the short text of the last card. last_card is never reset in new_chat() or set_mode(). After a chat clear or a mode switch, the same error within 20 s therefore adds no card, and cm_last_of finds none, so the short text falls back to S_E_GENERIC and no 'Повторить' button appears. The effect is minor and needs two errors close together, so I rate it low.

title: After D → 'Показать подсказки', the first-use hints never go away again
scenario: scr_about.c:132 sets only the UI subject (g_s_hints = 3). The app's s_a.hints is already 0 after three successful turns, and on_result posts UI_SET_HINTS only while s_a.hints > 0. The H bottom hint, 'Нажмите — стоп' while speaking and the busy-press hint therefore stay until reboot, and app status reports hints 0.
fix: Route the reset through the app (a UI_IN event that sets s_a.hints = 3), or have the app decrement from the UI's current value.
verify_note: scr_about.c:132 sets only the UI subject g_s_hints=3. The app's s_a.hints is the only counter that goes down (app.c:840-842, only while it is above 0), and it reaches 0 after three successful turns. After D → 'Показать подсказки' nothing ever sends UI_SET_HINTS again, so the hints stay until reboot. That contradicts ui.md 1250-1253, which says the counter drops by 1 per successful turn and is reset.

title: The model context is reset after idle with no divider, because the app and the AI client measure idle from different events
scenario: maybe_divider measures idle from last_end_t, which is also updated by a 'Не расслышал' gate reject, an unheard result, a cancel or a replay. hist_touch on the AI side measures from s_last_ms, which is updated only by hist_add after a successful exchange. Example: a successful question at t0, a press with nothing said at t0+8 min ('Не расслышал'), then a follow-up at t0+11 min ('А сколько ему было лет?'). The app sees 3 min idle and shows no divider, but the AI client sees 11 min and silently clears the history, so the model loses the context while the chat looks continuous.
fix: Use one idle rule: update last_end_t only on successful exchanges, or show the divider whenever ai_client_history_len() was cleared by the AI side (for example, compare before and after the submit).
verify_note: maybe_divider uses s_a.last_end_t. That value is also set by gate rejects (app.c:661), cancels (955) and replay finishes, and it is stamped after the speech ends. hist_touch (ai_history.c:60) measures from s_last_ms, which hist_add sets only after a successful assistant exchange, at result time. The two clocks drift apart. In the given scenario the app sees less than 10 min idle and shows no divider, while the AI client sees more than 10 min and silently clears the history. The model loses context while the chat looks continuous. This only happens near the idle boundary, so I rate it low.

title: Wi-Fi retry timer callback overflows the 2 KB timer-task stack, so the device crashes on every Wi-Fi drop
scenario: retry_cb runs in the FreeRTOS timer task ('Tmr Svc'), whose stack is CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH=2048 bytes (sdkconfig line 2262, not overridden). It calls connect_best_saved(), which has net_ap_t aps[16] (576 B, line 142) on the stack and then calls net_scan(), which adds wifi_ap_record_t recs[20] (about 1.8 KB, line 315), blocks up to 4 s in xEventGroupWaitBits and then calls start_sta(). Those frames alone are over 2.4 KB. Trigger: a saved network exists and the router reboots or goes out of range, or the board boots with its saved AP absent. WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED arms s_retry_timer, the callback runs 1-2 s later and overflows the stack. The result is either a canary panic or heap corruption next to the stack, then a reboot. It happens after READY, so s_rtc_reached_ready=1 and the crash counter never reaches safe mode: with the saved AP unavailable the board reboot-loops about every 10 s indefinitely. The callback also holds s_lock and blocks the timer service for up to 4 s.
fix: Do no scanning or connecting in the timer callback. Have retry_cb only notify a worker task with an internal stack of at least 4-6 KB (or post an event), and run connect_best_saved there. Alternatively put the scan records on the heap and raise CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH to 4096 or more, but blocking 4 s in the timer service should still go.
verify_note: Confirmed from the code and the built ELF. retry_cb (net.c:159) runs on the FreeRTOS timer task, and CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH=2048 is not overridden in sdkconfig.defaults. The disassembly gives these frame sizes: prvTimerTask entry 64, prvProcessExpiredTimer 32, retry_cb 32, connect_best_saved$part$0 0x280 (640 B), net_scan 0x7c0 (1984 B, mostly recs[20] at 92 B each). That is about 2.75 KB before xEventGroupWaitBits, esp_wifi_* or ESP_LOGI add their own frames, well past 2 KB. The callback is armed on every STA_DISCONNECTED while s_auto is set (router drop, saved AP missing at boot), and also by net_connect() failing (for example a wrong password), so the timer stack overflows into the memory next to it. The canary is CONFIG_FREERTOS_CHECK_STACKOVERFLOW_CANARY, and there is no end-of-stack watchpoint. The result is heap corruption plus a canary panic. Boot reaches selftest_ready before the 2 s retry fires, so the crash counter is cleared and a missing AP gives a reboot loop.

title: UI_IN_SLEEP is fed back as user activity, so dimming, ambient and screen-off are undone at once
scenario: ui_sleep enter(1) sets s_level=1, starts the dim fade and calls ui_emit(UI_IN_SLEEP,1). ui_input_cb posts EV_UI, and handle() runs app_io_activity() for every EV_UI (line 1322) before on_ui. The app still mirrors APP_SCREEN_ON and more than 1 s has passed since s_last_wake_post, so app_io.c:139-141 posts UI_WAKE. ui_sleep_wake() then restores full backlight and restarts the idle timer, so the screen never stays dimmed and never reaches ambient or off. Screen-off is worse: PWR short on idle Home calls app_io_screen_off(), which posts UI_SCREEN_OFF and sets s_screen=OFF. enter(3) emits UI_IN_SLEEP(3), and ui_input_cb sees app_io_screen()!=ON and posts EV_WAKE (line 1458-1461). app_io_activity() then calls screen_set(ON), which posts UI_WAKE, so the screen turns back on within milliseconds. The 'USB power' note flow (dim_tick -> screen_set(OFF)) is undone the same way, and that path also re-latches GPIO7. Result: on battery the display never sleeps.
fix: Treat UI_IN_SLEEP as a status report, not input. In ui_input_cb, handle UI_IN_SLEEP before the 'screen not on -> EV_WAKE' check and post it without EV_WAKE. In handle(), skip app_io_activity() for EV_UI whose i is UI_IN_SLEEP; only real user inputs should count as activity.
verify_note: Confirmed. enter() (ui_sleep.c:114) calls ui_emit(UI_IN_SLEEP), which synchronously calls ui_input_cb. UI_IN_SLEEP has no case in the switch, so it is posted as EV_UI. handle() runs app_io_activity() for every EV_UI (app.c:1322) before on_ui mirrors the level. At that point s_screen is still ON and more than 1 s has passed since s_last_wake_post (idle was at least dim_s), so UI_WAKE is posted. ui_sleep_wake() then restores level 0 at full backlight and emits SLEEP(0), and ui_input_cb sees DIM and posts EV_WAKE. The display therefore never stays dimmed or reaches ambient. For screen-off, app_io_screen_off sets OFF, the UI emits SLEEP(3), ui_input_cb sees a non-ON screen and posts EV_WAKE, and app_io_activity calls screen_set(ON), which posts UI_WAKE. The USB-note screen_set(OFF) in dim_tick fails the same way, and there app_io_activity also calls board_power_latch_on() because s_latch_off is set.

title: poll_touch counts artificial LVGL activity as user activity and re-latches power after PWR-long power-off
scenario: On battery, PWR held 3 s calls app_io_power_off(): board_power_off() releases GPIO7 and s_latch_off=true. The board only stays alive while the key is held. The UI is not told (no UI_SCREEN_OFF), so ui_sleep stays at level 0. On any never_sleeps() screen (keyboard/text entry, QR portal, adjust, dialog, onboarding, Wi-Fi connecting), ui_sleep tick_cb calls lv_display_trigger_activity() every second (ui_sleep.c:170-172). Within 200 ms poll_touch sees lv_display_get_inactive_time() < 250 and calls app_io_activity(). That re-runs board_power_latch_on() (line 133-137) and screen_set(ON). If the user is still holding PWR at that moment (usually the case for up to about 1 s), the board does not power off on release. It keeps running on battery with backlight 0, and the app believes the screen is on.
fix: While s_latch_off is set, ignore poll_touch activity and re-latch only on a real button press or a touch reported through the indev. Also post UI_SCREEN_OFF from app_io_power_off. Better: do not use lv_display_get_inactive_time as an activity source when ui_sleep resets it artificially (use a dedicated 'real input' timestamp).
verify_note: Confirmed. app_io_power_off releases the latch, sets s_latch_off and s_screen=OFF, and posts nothing to the UI, so ui_sleep stays at level 0. On never_sleeps() contexts (TEXT/QR/ADJUST/DIALOG/ONBOARD/WIFI_CONN), tick_cb calls lv_display_trigger_activity every 1 s. poll_touch runs every 200 ms with a 250 ms threshold, so it always sees idle<250 within about 200 ms of each trigger. It then calls app_io_activity(), which runs board_power_latch_on() and screen_set(ON). The backlight stays 0 because ui_sleep_wake at level 0 only triggers activity. If PWR is still held at that moment, which can be up to about 1.2 s after LONG, the board keeps running on battery with a black screen while the app reports ON. This is limited to those screens, so medium is the right severity.

title: Translator language change is only debounced while app and AI read the old pair from settings
scenario: ui_set_langs() updates g_lang_a/b (pill, chips, bubbles) and emits UI_IN_LANGS, but writes tr_lang_a/tr_lang_b only through ui_save_str. That write waits 1.5 s, and save_timer_cb (ui_work.c:247) keeps deferring it up to 20 s while the UI state is REC/UPLOAD/THINK/SPEAK. The app (tr_langs() at app.c:301-302, used for the forced chip source and the result side) and ai_client_submit (cfg_str tr_lang_a/b) read the settings, not the UI copy. Scenario: tap chip B, pick DE instead of EN, back on Home hold chip A within 1.5 s. Recording starts, the save is deferred for the whole turn, and the clip is translated RU->EN with an EN voice. Meanwhile the UI shows 'RU -> DE' (set_side uses the new g_lang codes). The app comment at app.c:1211 ('were saved by the UI') is false at that moment.
fix: Call ui_save_flush() in ui_set_langs (as is done for credentials), or carry the pair with UI_IN_LANGS: keep it in s_a and pass lang_a/lang_b explicitly in ai_request_t and to tr_langs(), so turns never depend on the debounced NVS copy.
verify_note: Confirmed. ui_set_langs (ui_misc.c:107) only calls ui_save_str, which uses a 1.5 s debounce, and save_timer_cb defers the write up to 20 s while the UI state is REC/UPLOAD/THINK/SPEAK. Both submit_clip and on-result tr_langs() (app.c:301) read settings_get_str. ai_client_submit falls back to cfg_str(tr_lang_a/b) because submit_clip never sets q.lang_a/lang_b. The UI_IN_LANGS handler only aborts and publishes. lp_cb is opened from the Home chip and navigates straight back, so picking a new B language and holding a chip within about 1.5 s translates with the old pair while the UI shows the new one.

title: lv_mem_monitor() walks the LVGL TLSF pool from the devcon task without the LVGL lock
scenario: print_heap_members() is used by 'heap' and 'info'. tools/smoke.py calls 'info' during runs. It calls lv_mem_monitor() directly on the devcon task. With LV_OS_NONE the builtin TLSF allocator has no locking, and taskLVGL allocates and frees draw tasks and layers every frame (42-46 fps). The pool walk (lv_tlsf_walk_pool following block sizes) races those splits and merges. At best the reported lvgl free, biggest and frag_pct are inconsistent. In a racing split or merge the walker can follow a stale size off a block and read outside the pool, which crashes the console task. selftest.c's lvgl_pool_ok() takes lvgl_port_lock for the same call; the console path does not.
fix: Take lvgl_port_lock(…, e.g. 200 ms) around lv_mem_monitor and omit the 'lvgl' member when the lock is not obtained, or collect the stats inside taskLVGL via lv_async_call.
verify_note: The race exists. print_heap_members calls lv_mem_monitor (verified in the ELF) on the devcon task (core 0) without lvgl_port_lock. lv_mem_monitor_core walks the TLSF pool with no lock, and with LV_OS_NONE the allocator mutex is a no-op anyway, while taskLVGL on core 1 allocates and frees every frame. In practice TLSF writes the split headers before resizing, and an absorbed block's stale header stays consistent until it is reused. A crash needs the walker to stall exactly on a header that is merged, reallocated and overwritten in that window, which is very unlikely. The realistic effect is inconsistent stats from a debug command, so I downgraded it to low.

title: settings_reset swaps and frees string values without s_lock (use-after-free or double free)
scenario: Factory reset (About -> reset_job on ui_work) or 'settings reset' frees each old s_val[i].str without taking s_lock. settings_get_str (ai/tts tasks mid-turn, cfg_str of ai_key/ai_url) copies under s_lock and can copy from the freed block, so a garbage key or URL can be sent in a request. settings_set_str on another task (portal /save on the httpd task, a console 'set') reads the same old pointer under the lock and frees it too. That double free corrupts the PSRAM heap and aborts with 'CORRUPT HEAP'. notify('*') also runs on the reset task while those readers are active.
fix: In settings_reset, take s_lock while replacing each pointer and free the old strings after giving the lock (same pattern as settings_set_str). Optionally serialize the NVS part of set/reset with one mutex.
verify_note: Confirmed that settings_reset (settings.c:254) swaps s_val[i].str and frees the old string without s_lock, while settings_get_str copies under the lock and settings_set_str swaps under it and then frees. Concurrent use can therefore read freed memory, or double-free if set_str runs on the same key at the same time. The window is microseconds, the About path reboots 300 ms later, and a concurrent set of the same key (portal or console) during a reset is very unlikely, so low is correct.

title: Reader-side xStreamBufferReset races the TTS writer and can replay stale audio after barge-in
scenario: audio_out_stop() only sets s_flush. play_task (prio 8, core 0) then calls xStreamBufferReset while the tts task (prio 5, also core 0) may be preempted inside xStreamBufferSend (wait 0, tts_client.c:149). The send path takes no lock: it reads xHead, copies, then stores xHead. If the reset lands between the read and the store, head is set to old_head+n with tail=0. The ring then reports old_head+n bytes 'available', and the speaker replays the whole previously played reply (up to 2 MB / about 43 s) right after the user interrupted. That audio is also captured by the recording that started on the barge-in. It is rare per stop but self-inflicted.
fix: Do not reset from the reader while a writer may be active. Either drain-and-discard in play_task (receive until empty) instead of xStreamBufferReset, or have the writer side perform the reset, or guard send and reset with a mutex.
verify_note: Confirmed against the IDF FreeRTOS source. prvWriteMessageToBuffer reads xHead, copies the data, then stores xHead with no lock. xStreamBufferReset only checks for blocked waiters, and none exist because out_write uses wait 0. play_task (prio 8, core 0) is woken from i2s_channel_write by the DMA ISR and can preempt tts (prio 5, core 0) in the middle of a send. If s_flush is pending at that point, the reset sets head=tail=0, then tts stores head=old_head+n and the stale ring contents replay. It needs a barge-in during the TTS download plus that preemption point, so it is rare.

title: UI picker GETs run as uncancellable sync jobs on the single ai task and block voice turns and the UI worker
scenario: Opening Models, Voices or Key info runs ai_run_sync(job_list/job_tts_list/job_key) on the ai task, with background retries 2+4+8 s through ai_sleep_ms(delay, NULL, NULL) (no abort) and up to 20 s per attempt (OR_TO_GET). On a stalled network that is about 90 s per page. A voice turn submitted meanwhile waits in s_q, and app.c's APP_TURN_MAX_MS (75 s) then cancels it with N8 'no result' although nothing was sent. The UI worker is blocked in ai_run_sync (portMAX_DELAY) the whole time, so later jobs queue behind it: debounced setting saves (a just-typed key), Wi-Fi scans, and the QR screen's stop_job. Leaving the phone-setup screen therefore leaves the SoftAP portal running, and app.c then refuses turns with 'Закройте настройку сети'.
fix: Give background jobs an abort callback (job_waiting() / a cancel generation) and pass it to or_exchange and ai_sleep_ms. Let ai_run_sync take a timeout, or give a queued JOB_TURN priority over sync jobs. Keep portal stop off the shared worker queue.
verify_note: The core claim is confirmed. ai_client_list_models, tts_models and key_info run through ai_run_sync (portMAX_DELAY) on the single ai task, called from the single ui_work worker. ai_get_json does up to 3 background retries (2/4/8 s) through ai_sleep_ms(delay, NULL, NULL) with no abort, and each attempt can take up to 20 s with OR_TO_GET. On a stalled relay that blocks queued turns (cut off by APP_TURN_MAX_MS) and all ui_work jobs, such as Wi-Fi scans and saves, for about 50-90 s. The portal part is overstated. stop_job is only delayed, not lost: start_done and delete_cb queue it in order. There is also no realistic way to start a models fetch while the portal is running, and a turn on a stalled network would fail anyway. That makes this a degraded-network latency issue, so low.

title: Portal /save responses contain double-encoded (mojibake) Russian text
scenario: Found outside this dimension. The string literals at lines 227, 233 and 239 are UTF-8 that was decoded as CP1251 and re-encoded (bytes D0 A0 D1 9B... = 'РћС€РёР±РєР°'). The phone that submits the setup form therefore shows 'РЎРѕС…СЂР°РЅРµРЅРѕ…' instead of 'Сохранено. Подключаюсь к «…»' and 'Ошибка в поле …'. The file also starts with a UTF-8 BOM. portal.html itself is clean.
fix: Re-save portal.c as plain UTF-8 without BOM and restore the literals 'Ошибка в поле %s', 'Сохранено. Подключаюсь к «%s»…' and 'Сохранено.'.
verify_note: Confirmed in HEAD. portal.c starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF), and the literals at lines 227, 233 and 239 are double-encoded: the bytes D0 A0 D1 9B... decode to 'РћС€РёР±РєР°…'. portal.html shows the /save response verbatim with s.textContent=t, so the phone displays mojibake for the save and error messages. The feature still works, so low.

title: /save changes ai_url to any https host while keeping the stored key; there is no Origin/Host/CSRF check and the AP PSK is only 8 digits
scenario: While the portal runs, someone sends POST /save with the body ai_url=https://evil.example/api/v1 and no ai_key. It can come from a second station that cracked the 8-digit numeric WPA2 PSK (line 290, 1e8 candidates, about a minute offline from the captured join handshake). It can also come from a cross-site form submit in another tab on the user's phone, since the request is a simple urlencoded POST and h_save checks only the local socket IP. settings_set_str accepts the new URL because it only checks the https:// prefix, and the key is kept. The next prewarm or turn sends Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-... to evil.example. That gets around the 'secrets never echoed' design.
fix: In h_save, require Host == 192.168.4.1 and a same-origin Origin/Referer, or a per-session token embedded in the served page. If the ai_url host changes and the same POST carries no ai_key, clear the stored key (or reject the change). Use a longer alphanumeric AP password.
verify_note: Confirmed in code. h_save (portal.c:206-213) stores any ai_url that passes settings_set_str, which only checks the https:// prefix (settings.c:180-181). It keeps the stored ai_key when the key field is empty. There is no Origin/Host/token check, only the local socket address check (from_ap). The 8-digit PSK at portal.c:290 is crackable offline from a captured handshake. So a station that joins the AP can point ai_url at its own host, and the next request sends the Bearer key there. The attacker has to be physically nearby during a short, user-started setup session. The cross-site route from another phone tab is speculative: the AP has no internet, and browsers' local-network-access restrictions apply. The 8-digit PSK and 'empty secret keeps stored value' are written into the spec. Low.

title: tts_key/stt_key fall back to the OpenRouter ai_key even when tts_url/stt_url point to a different host
scenario: The requirements say every endpoint can use its own service. A user runs `set tts_url https://piper.home.example/v1` (a keyless self-hosted or third-party TTS) and leaves tts_key empty. cfg_key (lines 79-85) returns ai_key. speak_chunk (tts_client.c:422-424) then sends Authorization: Bearer <OpenRouter key> to that host on every TTS chunk. stt_client.c:44-46 does the same for stt_url. The OpenRouter key leaks to an unrelated server.
fix: Fall back to ai_key only when the effective tts_url/stt_url is empty or has the same origin as ai_url. Otherwise send no Authorization header, or fail with K0.
verify_note: cfg_key (ai_util.c:79-85) falls back to ai_key whenever tts_key/stt_key is empty, whatever the host. speak_chunk (tts_client.c:422-424) and stt_transcribe_ex (stt_client.c:44-46) then send it as the bearer to the configured tts_url/stt_url. Setting tts_url to another host with no tts_key therefore sends the OpenRouter key to that host. The fallback is documented ('"" → ai_*', architecture.md:467). It only happens after the user deliberately points an endpoint at a different service. That service is one the user chose, and it is reached over TLS. Real, but low impact.

title: Factory reset erases only NVS namespace "cfg": Wi-Fi passwords survive and the old key stays readable in flash
scenario: The user runs About -> 'Сброс настроек' / 'Factory reset' (scr_about.c:109), or `settings reset`, before giving the device away. settings_reset calls nvs_erase_all only on "cfg". Saved SSIDs and passwords in namespace "wifi" (net.c:18, 79-95) stay, and the device reconnects to the home network after the reset. architecture.md:429 specifies settings_reset(bool keep_wifi), and the code ignores Wi-Fi entirely. nvs_erase_all also only marks entries as erased: the sk-or-v1 key and ai_url bytes stay in the NVS pages. The flash is not encrypted and ROM download mode is on, so `esptool read-flash 0x9000 0x6000` recovers them.
fix: For a factory reset, run nvs_flash_deinit + nvs_flash_erase (the whole partition, which physically erases the sectors) and then restart. Alternatively erase "wifi" as well, clear net's RAM list, and erase the NVS partition sectors. Implement the documented keep_wifi option for the console variant.
verify_note: settings_reset (settings.c:245-263) erases only the "cfg" namespace. Wi-Fi networks and passwords live in the separate "wifi" namespace (net.c:18, 79-95), and nothing in the reset touches them. After About → 'Сброс настроек' / 'Factory reset' (scr_about.c:106-111) or console `settings reset`, net_start reloads the saved networks (net.c:226, 233) and reconnects. The spec (architecture.md:429, 1341: `settings_reset(bool keep_wifi)`, `settings reset [keep_wifi]`) means a reset without keep_wifi should clear Wi-Fi, and onboarding after a factory reset includes the network step (ui.md:273). The kept passwords sit in plain NVS. The point that nvs_erase_all leaves erased key bytes in flash is also correct, because NVS encryption is off on purpose. The about-screen dialog mentions only key/model/settings, but the English label and the spec promise a full reset.

title: OTA image is marked VALID before Wi-Fi/AI/app start; the documented soft-stage-2 rollback is missing and crash loops after READY never reach safe mode
scenario: An image pushed with `ota push` has a bug in app_start, net_start or TLS, for example a NULL dereference in the app task 2 s after boot, or every HTTPS request failing. selftest_run (line 93) confirms it before lines 95-103 run, so the bootloader never rolls it back. architecture.md:1408 says that after 3 failed HTTPS attempts the UI offers 'Откатить прошивку?', but nothing calls ota_rollback_now. For a crash after READY, selftest_ready (selftest.c:207-208) has already set reached_ready=1 and crashes=0, so the counter never grows and safe mode never starts. The result is an endless reboot loop on a VALID image that only USB recovery can fix.
fix: Implement soft stage 2: keep a 'probation' flag in RTC/NVS for the first N minutes after a new version's first boot. Count crashes after READY during probation and call ota_rollback_now (or offer it in the UI) after repeated crashes or 3 failed HTTPS attempts to ai_url.
verify_note: Partly real. Confirming the image before net_start/app_start is the specified order (architecture.md §8.1 step 6-7). Not counting crashes after READY is also by design (selftest.c:51, 207: safe mode is for crashes during boot). The real gap is that the documented soft stage 2 (architecture.md:1408) is not implemented: nothing calls ota_rollback_now (only ota.c/ota.h reference it), so the UI never offers 'Откатить прошивку?' after 3 failed HTTPS attempts. Recovery still exists. `ota rollback` on the console works while the device stays up, and a crash loop is covered by the documented USB/download-mode runbook. OTA images arrive through the dev console anyway. Low.

title: URL settings accept whitespace, and esp_http_client then logs the full URL with the secret at ERROR level
scenario: settings_set_str checks only the "https://" prefix. An ai_url with a trailing space is stored as-is, for example from the portal (url_decode turns '+' into ' ') or from the device keyboard (UI_FIELD_URL validation also checks only the prefix). Every request then reaches esp_http_client_set_url, where http_parser rejects the space and IDF prints `E HTTP_CLIENT: Error parse url https://host/<secret>/api/v1 /chat/completions` (esp_http_client.c:1252). orconn.c:55 keeps HTTP_CLIENT at ERROR on purpose, so the secret appears in the console log on every prewarm or turn.
fix: Reject or trim whitespace and control characters (and anything outside the RFC 3986 URL set) in settings_set_str for the *_url keys. Optionally set the HTTP_CLIENT log level to NONE, since orhttp already reports errors itself.
verify_note: Confirmed. settings_set_str checks only the https:// prefix and the length. The portal's url_decode turns '+' into a space. UI_FIELD_URL accepts printable ASCII including spaces and checks only the prefix (ui_kb.c:337-338). A trailing space makes ai_join_url build 'https://host/<secret>/api/v1 /chat/completions'. IDF's http_parser rejects the space (normal_url_char[32] = 0), and esp_http_client_set_url logs 'Error parse url <full url>' at ERROR (esp_http_client.c:1252). orconn.c:55 keeps HTTP_CLIENT at ERROR. This breaks the project's own rule in orhttp.h:58 ('never logged: it may carry a relay secret'), and every AI request fails. The log goes only to the local console, so low.

title: `net get <url> auth` attaches the API key to plain http:// URLs
scenario: The help text says <https-url>, but cmd_net does not check the scheme, and neither does httpx_client. A typo such as `net get http://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key auth` sends Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-... in cleartext before any redirect to https. This is the only path where the key can leave the device without TLS.
fix: Reject non-https URLs in cmd_net, at least when `auth` is given, the same way ota_start_https does.
verify_note: Confirmed. cmd_net (cmd_net.c:134-147) passes argv[2] to httpx_probe without checking the scheme. httpx_client (httpx.c:14-34) adds 'Authorization: Bearer <ai_key>' for any URL, so `net get http://... auth` sends the key in cleartext. Every other path forces https (settings_set_str for *_url, ota url). It needs a typo in a dev-console command that also includes `auth`, so low.

title: stop_dns_server deletes the DNS task while it is blocked in recvfrom: the socket leaks, port 53 stays bound, and captive DNS is dead on later portal sessions
scenario: portal_stop -> stop_dns_server sets started=false and calls vTaskDelete right away. The task sits in recvfrom with no timeout (line 225), so close() never runs. On the next portal_start, the new task's bind to :53 fails (only logged at line 217) and recvfrom on the unbound socket never gets data. Phones that rely on DNS-based captive detection no longer get the auto-popup until reboot. Each session also leaks one of the 16 LWIP sockets, which the HTTPS pool needs.
fix: Set SO_RCVTIMEO on the socket and let the task exit and close the socket itself when started==false (stop waits for it), or close the socket from stop_dns_server before deleting the task.
verify_note: Confirmed. stop_dns_server (dns_server.c:291-298) sets started=false and calls vTaskDelete on a task blocked in recvfrom with no timeout (line 225), so close() never runs and the socket stays bound to INADDR_ANY:53. On the next portal_start (scr_qr.c:93 or the `portal start` console command), the new socket has no SO_REUSEADDR and bind fails with EADDRINUSE. That is only logged, and 'Socket bound' is still printed. recvfrom on the unbound socket never returns, and the leaked socket's recvmbox (size 6) fills and drops queries. Captive DNS is dead until reboot, and each session leaks one of the 16 lwIP sockets. The URL QR step and DHCP option 114 remain as fallbacks, so low.

title: Portal /save replies are double-encoded (mojibake) Russian text
scenario: The string literals at lines 227, 233 and 239 contain UTF-8 that was re-encoded through CP1251 (bytes d0 a0 d1 9b... = "РћС€РёР±РєР°"). After 'Сохранить', the phone shows "РЎРѕС…СЂР°РЅРµРЅРѕ. РџРѕРґРєР»СЋС‡Р°СЋСЃСЊ Рє В«HomeВ»вЂ¦". The field-error reply 'Ошибка в поле ai_url' is unreadable too. This is outside the security dimension but is in the portal.
fix: Re-save portal.c as UTF-8 with the correct literals ("Ошибка в поле %s", "Сохранено. Подключаюсь к «%s»…", "Сохранено."), or use \u-escaped / \x byte literals.
verify_note: Confirmed in the committed file. The bytes at portal.c:227 start with d0a0 d19b d0a1 e282ac, which is the UTF-8 for 'Ошибка' wrongly decoded as CP1251 and saved again as UTF-8 ('РћС€РёР±РєР°'). Lines 233 and 239 are the same. The handler sends them as text/plain; charset=utf-8, and portal.html sets status.textContent from the response. So every portal save shows unreadable text to the Russian-speaking user: the success message, the connecting-to-SSID message and the field-error message. The save itself works, so not high, but it happens on every use of the main setup path.

title: Translator offers Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic, but the fonts cannot show them, so their text is erased
scenario: The user opens Chip B -> LP and picks Китайский (zh). The translator prompt asks for native script with no transliteration. Every chat text goes through cm_set -> sanitized_copy -> ui_str_sanitize(..., &ui_20) (ui_chat.c:134), and that function drops every glyph ui_20 lacks. The fonts cover only Latin, Latin Extended and Cyrillic, with no fallback font. So an RU->ZH turn shows the Russian transcript and an empty line 3, a ZH->RU turn shows an empty transcript, and RD shows an empty box. With no speaker (requirement 5) the translation cannot be seen at all. ja, ko and ar behave the same way.
fix: Limit the LP language table to scripts that ui_16/20/28 can render (the ui.md 3.7 list). Alternatively add CJK and Arabic fallback fonts, or ask the model for a romanised line for those languages.
verify_note: Confirmed. The table at main/ui/ui_misc.c:53-59 offers zh/ja/ko/ar in LP (scr_mode.c:258 loops over all of them). The font headers show ui_16/20/28 cover only 0x20-0x17F, 0x218-0x21B, 0x400-0x4FF and some punctuation, with .fallback = NULL. cm_set/cm_append -> sanitized_copy -> ui_str_sanitize(..., &ui_20) (ui_chat.c:134, ui_str.c:385) drops every code point the font lacks. The prompt forbids transliteration (ai_prompts.c:49). The display_text romanisation that ui.md:210 plans is not in the code at all. So CJK and Arabic transcripts and translations show as empty bubbles and an empty RD box. Without a speaker the translation cannot be seen.

title: While a persistent fault is shown, the mode sheet cannot be opened, and in translator mode neither can Settings
scenario: The pill is the only way into M, which holds mode switching, typed questions and history. While g_s_fault is set or the device is offline, pill_cb opens the fix screen instead of M. In translator mode both side buttons are language chips, so Settings is unreachable too. Example: credit runs out in translator mode (402 -> UI_FAULT_NO_CREDIT). The pill opens KEYINFO, which has only info rows. The card's 'Подробнее' also opens KEYINFO. The chips open LP. The user cannot switch to assistant mode, change the key or provider, or change volume or brightness. The fault clears only after a successful turn, so the device stays locked until a reboot. Offline in H' opens only W. In assistant mode with any fault, the mode cannot be switched at all, because S has no mode row.
fix: Always keep a route to M while a fault is shown, for example a 'fix' row at the top of M while the pill still shows the fault, or a long-press on the pill. Also add Provider and Settings links on KEYINFO, W and D when they are opened as fault fixes.
verify_note: Confirmed. pill_cb (scr_home.c:980) opens UI_OPEN_FAULT_FIX whenever g_s_fault != NONE or the device is offline. In translator mode both side buttons are chips that open LP (side_cb), so M and S cannot be reached. The fix screens have no route back. NO_CREDIT -> KEYINFO, which has info rows only (scr_ai.c:459-480); the spec 5.6 says P. MIC -> About. Offline -> W. S has no mode row. g_s_fault is cleared only by a successful turn or a key/model setting change (app.c:828, 1171-1175), not by topping up credit. The device is not fully locked: a successful turn after a top-up, or a reboot (the fault is RAM only), clears the fault. That is why medium rather than high.

title: 'Проверить звук' and 'Диагностика' open About, which has no sound test, mic test or speaker switch
scenario: With Динамик = Нет, the user taps the voice button. The card 'Динамик не подключён' appears with the button 'Проверить звук', which runs ui_open_card -> UI_SCR_ABOUT. The same happens for the MIC card ('Диагностика') and the 'Микрофон ›' fault pill (ui.c:346). scr_about_build lists firmware, network and memory information plus touch test, hints, licences, restart and reset. It has no mic or speaker test (ui.md 3.7 D) and no speaker on/off switch. The action leads nowhere useful, and the user cannot fix the reported problem from there.
fix: Add the 'Тест микрофона' (live level) and 'Тест динамика' rows to D. Alternatively route NO_SPEAKER to Settings -> Динамик and MIC to a mic-level screen.
verify_note: Confirmed. ui_open_card maps UI_CARD_MIC and UI_CARD_NO_SPEAKER to UI_SCR_ABOUT (ui.c:362-363), and UI_FAULT_MIC also goes to ABOUT (ui.c:346). The cards' buttons read 'Диагностика' and 'Проверить звук' (ui_chat.c:516-517, ui_str.c:88/92). scr_about_build has only info rows plus touch test, hints, licences, restart and reset (scr_about.c:201-205). It has no mic level or speaker test, although ui.md:586-587 requires them, and no speaker switch.

title: Answering 'Есть динамик' in onboarding leaves voice replies off, because text_only defaults to 1
scenario: settings_table.inc sets text_only to 1 by default. On first boot, O4 asks 'Подключён ли динамик?' and the user taps 'Есть динамик'. set_speaker(true) only sets g_s_speaker; it changes text_only only in the 'no speaker' branch. As a result, voice_on() is false and the assistant and the translator never speak (requirements 1 and 2) until the user finds the voice toggle. Settings -> Динамик switched from Нет back to Подключён does not turn voice back on either.
fix: In set_speaker(true), and when S -> Динамик is turned on, set text_only = 0 (ui_set, UI_IN_TEXT_ONLY, ui_save_int). Alternatively default text_only to 0 and let 'Нет динамика' turn it on.
verify_note: Confirmed. settings_table.inc:5 sets the text_only default to 1, and ui_init loads it into g_s_text_only. set_speaker(true) in scr_onboard.c:155-167 only sets g_s_speaker and emits UI_IN_SPEAKER. It changes text_only only when on is false. After 'Есть динамик' on a fresh device, voice_on() (app.c:408) is false, so neither TTS mode speaks. R_SPEAKER turned back on in S (scr_settings.c:119-131) does not clear text_only either.

title: The 'no speaker' choice is lost on reboot
scenario: The user picks 'Нет динамика' in O4, or turns S -> Динамик to Нет. g_s_speaker and the app's s_no_speaker are RAM only. No settings key exists for them and nothing posts UI_SET_SPEAKER at boot. After a restart, Settings shows 'Динамик: Подключён', the warning dot on the voice button is gone and RD 'Повторить' is enabled again. If the user taps the voice button, voice turns on: every reply then waits for paid TTS (THINK, then up to 2.5 s hidden text) and the purple SPEAKING orb plays silent audio. Requirement 5 (no speaker) breaks after any reboot.
fix: Persist the flag (for example a 'speaker' U8 setting), read it in ui_init and app_start, and save it from set_speaker and R_SPEAKER.
verify_note: Confirmed. s_no_speaker (app.c:404) and g_s_speaker are RAM only. ui_init always sets g_s_speaker = 1, and its comment at ui.c:666-668 admits that no stored flag exists. The settings table has no speaker key, and nothing posts UI_SET_SPEAKER 0 at boot. After a reboot, S shows 'Подключён', the warning dot is gone and RD replay is enabled. A tap on the voice button then enables TTS on a device with no speaker.

title: The reader's 'Повторить' and 'Не тот язык' (and old retry cards) act on the latest turn, not the one shown
scenario: replay() speaks s_a.last_tr and ignores the entry id that the reader sends (UI_IN_REPLAY arg). rerun_clip() re-sends s_a.clip_*, the most recent recording, and text_turn() never clears clip_ok. Example: turn 1 is spoken, turn 2 is typed, then the user opens the turn 2 bubble in RD and taps 'Не тот язык'. The device re-sends turn 1's audio with the source forced to the other language. Opening an older bubble and tapping 'Повторить' speaks the newest translation instead. After any recording that was not heard, clip_ok is false and the button only says 'Пока недоступно'. Retry stadiums on older error cards also re-send whatever was recorded last.
fix: Keep the clip or text and the translation per chat entry id, or at least compare the RD entry id with the kept turn. Disable or hide 'Не тот язык' and 'Повторить' when the shown entry is not the kept one, instead of acting on another turn.
verify_note: Confirmed. RD can open for any CM_TURN entry (scr_home.c:508, scr_hist.c:35). replay_cb sends the entry id, but replay() (app.c:783-806) ignores it and always speaks s_a.last_tr. wrong_cb -> UI_IN_WRONG_LANG -> rerun_clip (app.c:747-762) re-sends s_a.clip_*, the most recent recording. text_turn never clears clip_ok, so 'Не тот язык' on a typed turn re-sends the previous voice clip. start_recording sets clip_ok=false (app.c:534), and a recording that is not heard never sets it back, so the button then says 'Пока недоступно'. Retry buttons on older cards call retry_last, which also uses the latest turn.

title: BOOT on the phone-setup (QR) screen shows a 'Закройте настройку сети' error instead of jumping home and recording
scenario: On Q, BOOT runs app_ptt_down -> ui_boot_down. That posts UI_GOTO HOME and returns true, and the app calls start_recording() at once. The UI has not left Q yet, and the portal stop runs later in the worker after Q is deleted, so ready() still sees portal_active() (app.c:375) and returns RDY_PORTAL. show_error('PT') then adds a generic 'Ошибка' card and puts the orb into ERROR, contradicting ui.md 2.3 ('jump to H and record'). The user has to press BOOT again.
fix: When ui_boot_down leaves Q, stop the portal synchronously first, or have the app defer the recording until the UI reports H (pending press). Alternatively make BOOT on Q only go home.
verify_note: Confirmed. For UI_CTX_QR, ui_boot_down (ui.c:544-565) only posts UI_GOTO HOME and returns true. app_ptt_down (app.c:999-1027) then calls start_recording at once on the app task. ready() checks app_io_portal() -> portal_active() first (app.c:375). The portal stops only after the Q screen is deleted asynchronously and stop_job runs on the UI worker (scr_qr.c:131-135, 313-316), so it is still active. show_not_ready(RDY_PORTAL) -> show_error('PT') posts a generic 'Ошибка' card and APP_ERROR. This contradicts ui.md 2.3 ('jump to H/H′ and record').

title: A changed translator language takes effect only after the debounced save, so a quick turn uses the old pair
scenario: In LP the user picks Deutsch for slot B. g_lang_b, the chips and the pill change at once, but tr_lang_b is written 1.5 s later, and later still while the app is busy. Both the app (tr_langs) and ai_client (cfg_str 'tr_lang_*') read the stored settings. If the user holds chip DE within that window, the request is sent with the old 'en' pair: the speech is translated to or from English while the bubble is labelled DE. The UI_IN_LANGS handler assumes the values are already saved.
fix: Call ui_save_flush() in ui_set_langs (as the key and URL do), or pass lang_a and lang_b explicitly in ai_request_t from the UI copy.
verify_note: Confirmed. ui_set_langs (ui_misc.c:99-110) updates g_lang_a/b and the chips at once but calls the debounced ui_save_str: a 1.5 s delay, deferred up to 20 s while REC/UPLOAD/THINK (ui_work.c:21-22, 245-255). submit_clip reads tr_langs() from settings (app.c:582) and does not pass lang_a/lang_b. ai_client then falls back to cfg_str('tr_lang_*') (ai_client.c:1067-1076). A chip hold within that window, or one that starts recording before the flush, uses the old pair.

title: Error card bodies and TTS error toasts are always Russian, even with the English UI
scenario: With Язык меню = English, a 5xx, TLS, 401 or missing-key error posts UI_ERROR with or_err_t.msg_ru as the card body. orerr.c has Russian texts only. on_tts_error toasts e->msg_ru, and KEYINFO shows j->e.msg_ru. An English-UI user therefore sees cards such as 'Server didn't respond' followed by a Russian body.
fix: Add English texts to orerr rows and choose by ui_str_lang(), or pass NULL bodies and use the localised card strings.
verify_note: Confirmed. or_err_t has only msg_ru/msg_retry_ru (orhttp.h:78-79), and orerr.c rows are Russian only. show_error passes msg_ru as the card body for rows with body=true (app.c:354, 370, 1271). TTS errors toast e->msg_ru (app.c:901), and KEYINFO shows j->e.msg_ru (scr_ai.c:411). With ui_lang=en, the card titles are English but the bodies are Russian.

title: A missing API key is shown as 'Ключ не принят' with a card that has no action
scenario: No key is set, for example after skipping onboarding by pressing PWR on O1, and the user talks. RDY_KEY leads to K0, which maps to UI_CARD_GENERIC with UI_FAULT_BAD_KEY. The pill says the key was rejected although none exists, and the card ('Ошибка / Нет API-ключа. Введите ключ в Настройках.') has no button to enter one.
fix: Map K0 to a card with an 'Ввести ключ' action that opens Provider or K hex, and use a 'Нет ключа' pill text.
verify_note: Confirmed. ERR_MAP maps K0 to UI_CARD_GENERIC with UI_FAULT_BAD_KEY (app.c:321). UI_CARD_GENERIC has no action (ui_chat.c:506), and the pill text is S_F_BAD_KEY 'Ключ не принят' (ui_str.c:62) although no key exists. The pill itself does route to Provider (ui.c:340-341), so a fix is still reachable. Low.

title: 'Лицо шара' is not saved, so it turns itself back on after reboot
scenario: S -> Лицо шара -> Выкл toggles g_s_face only. No settings key exists and ui_init always starts with g_s_face = 1, so after a restart the face is back.
fix: Add a 'face' setting, save it on toggle and read it in ui_init.
verify_note: Confirmed. R_FACE only toggles g_s_face (scr_settings.c:135-138), and nothing saves it. The settings table has no 'face' key, and ui_init always creates g_s_face with value 1 (ui.c:676). The choice is lost on reboot.

title: Clearing history from Settings throws the user out of Settings to Home
scenario: S -> История -> 'Удалить' runs clear_history, which emits UI_IN_NEW_CHAT. The app's new_chat() then posts UI_GOTO HOME, which drops the Settings stack. The toast 'История очищена' (top layer) is left floating over H's side buttons for 2 s.
fix: Post UI_GOTO HOME only for the M/HIST 'Новый разговор' paths, or let clear_history reset the AI context without navigating.
verify_note: Confirmed. clear_history (scr_settings.c:90-98) emits UI_IN_NEW_CHAT. The app's new_chat (app.c:1126-1133) posts UI_GOTO HOME, and nav_goto -> ui_nav_home drops the Settings stack. The user leaves S after confirming the delete. The toast is shown before the jump, on the chrome toast layer.

title: A hidden open network cannot be joined from 'Другая сеть…'
scenario: ssid_done always calls ask_password(). The UI_FIELD_WIFI_PASS rule needs at least 8 characters, so OK stays disabled with an empty password. A hidden network with no password can only be set up from a phone.
fix: Allow an empty password in the password step opened from 'Другая сеть…' (or add an 'Открытая сеть' option), and connect with "".
verify_note: Confirmed. ssid_done (scr_wifi.c:184-190) always calls ask_password(). UI_FIELD_WIFI_PASS has min_len 8 (ui_kb.c:291, enforced at line 348), so an empty password cannot be confirmed. Hidden open networks cannot be joined on the device. They are rare.

title: With volume at 0, voice is silently off and the reader's replay says 'Нет динамика'
scenario: The user sets volume to 0 in A. voice_on() returns false, so no TTS plays, yet the voice button still shows the speaker icon and gives no hint. In RD, 'Повторить' toasts S_E_SPK 'Нет динамика' although a speaker is connected and the actual cause is volume 0.
fix: Show a 'Громкость 0' message instead of 'Нет динамика', and reflect volume 0 in the voice button and status.
verify_note: Confirmed. replay() toasts S_E_SPK when volume == 0 (app.c:790-792), and S_E_SPK is 'Нет динамика' / 'No speaker' (ui_str.c:101). That message is misleading when a speaker is connected. voice_on() treats volume 0 as off (app.c:408), and the home voice button reflects only text_only and speaker. The volume-0-as-text-only behaviour is intended by architecture.md:449, but the wrong message and the missing indication are real.

title: Chat history (HIST) is lost on every reboot, although ui.md 3.3 says it is kept
scenario: ui.md 3.3 says storage keeps 40 messages per mode in PSRAM, persisted to the storage partition, and shown in HIST. The cm ring exists only in PSRAM and nothing writes or loads it. After a power cycle, M -> История and the translator RD history are empty.
fix: Persist the per-mode ring (for example a file on the storage partition, written while idle) and load it in cm_init, or drop the claim from the spec.
verify_note: Confirmed. ui.md:447 says the 40 messages per mode are 'persisted to the storage partition'. cm rings live only in PSRAM (ui_chat.h:25), and the code has no file or partition I/O at all: the only 'storage' match is esp_wifi_set_storage. After a power cycle, HIST and the RD history are empty.
